lesson.subject: math

misconceptionProbe.signal: Ava thinks odd numbers can have equal pairs.
misconceptionProbe.checkPrompt: If 5 robots stand in pairs, does one robot have no partner?
misconceptionProbe.expectedConfusion: Thinking every number can be split into two equal groups without leftovers.

blocks.title: Robot Teams
blocks.prompt: Ava, let's help the space robots find partners for their mission!

blocks.title: Even or Odd?
blocks.prompt: Even numbers have partners. Odd numbers always have one left over.

blocks.title: Sort the Robots
blocks.prompt: Drag the robot groups to the Even or Odd landing pads.

blocks.title: Star Check
blocks.prompt: There are 7 stars. Is 7 even or odd?

blocks.title: Mission Complete
blocks.prompt: Ava practiced identifying even and odd numbers using robot pairs.

sceneSpec.title: Magic Garden
sceneSpec.instruction: Choose rows and columns, then plant the seeds to make a glowing array.
sceneSpec.helperText: Count the rows first. Then count how many are in each row.
sceneSpec.rewardFact: Rows and columns help your eyes see totals faster.

hintLadder.text: Try drawing circles around pairs of robots to see if any are alone.
If you have 3 robots, can they all have a partner?
4 is even because 2+2=4. Now look at 5. Is it even?

lesson.parentSummary: Ava explored even and odd numbers by pairing 'space robots'. She learned that even numbers form perfect pairs, while odd numbers have one left over.
